arxiv-2102-04452.title: Topological Quantum Computing and 3-Manifolds
arxiv-2102-04452.creator: Torsten Asselmeyer-Maluga
arxiv-2102-04452.description: Abstract In this paper, we will present some ideas to use 3D topology for quantum computing. Topological quantum computing in the usual sense works with an encoding of information as knotted quantum states of topological phases of matter, thus being locked into topology to prevent decay. Today, the basic structure is a 2D system to realize anyons with braiding operations.

arxiv-2103-02341.title: A Study of the Separating Property in Reed-Solomon Codes by Bounding the Minimum Distance
arxiv-2103-02341.creator: Marcel Fernandez and Jorge J. Urroz
arxiv-2103-02341.description: Abstract . According to their strength, the tracing properties of a code can be categorized as frameproof, separating, IPP and TA. It is known that if the minimum distance of the code is larger than a certain threshold then the TA property implies the rest. Silverberg et al.

arxiv-2103-15811.title: On eigenvalues of symmetric matrices with PSD principal submatrices
arxiv-2103-15811.creator: Khazhgali Kozhasov
arxiv-2103-15811.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Khazhgali Kozhasov. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 14P10, 15A18, 15B57, 90C22 Abstract. We investigate convexity properties of the set of eigenvalue tuples of n\times n real symmetric matrices, whose all k\times k (where k\leq n is fixed) minors are positive semidefinite. It is proven that the set \lambda({\mathcal{S}}^{n,k}) of eigenvalue vectors of all such matrices is star-shaped with respect to the nonnegative orthant \mathbb{R}^{n}_{\geq 0} and not convex already when (n,k)=(4,2) .

arxiv-2201-06928.title: Thermal Relaxation and Cooling of Quark Stars with a Strangelet Crust
arxiv-2201-06928.creator: Joas Zapata, Rodrigo Negreiros, Thiago Sales, Prashanth Jaikumar
arxiv-2201-06928.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Joas Zapata, Rodrigo Negreiros, Thiago Sales, Prashanth Jaikumar. In this article, we explore the cooling of isolated quark stars. These objects are structured of a homogeneous quark matter core and crusted by matter. To do this, we adopt two kinds of crust: (i) a crust made of purely nuclear matter following the Baym-Pethick-Sutherland (BPS) equation of state (EoS) and (ii) a crust made of nuggets of strange quark matter (strangelets).

arxiv-2210-06618.title: QMRNet: Quality Metric Regression for EO Image Quality Assessment and Super-Resolution
arxiv-2210-06618.creator: David Berga, Pau Gallés, Katalin Takáts, Eva Mohedano, Laura Riordan-Chen, Clara Garcia-Moll, David Vilaseca, Javier Marín
arxiv-2210-06618.description: Abstract Latest advances in Super-Resolution (SR) have been tested with general purpose images such as faces, landscapes and objects, mainly unused for the task of super-resolving Earth Observation (EO) images. In this research paper, we benchmark state-of-the-art SR algorithms for distinct EO datasets using both Full-Reference and No-Reference Image Quality Assessment (IQA) metrics.

arxiv-2305-11297.title: Planetesimal formation via the streaming instability with multiple grain sizes 2020 Planetesimal formation via the streaming instability with multiple grain sizes – References
arxiv-2305-11297.creator: J. J. Rucska, J. W. Wadsley
arxiv-2305-11297.description: Abstract Kilometre-sized planetesimals form from pebbles of a range of sizes. We present the first simulations of the streaming instability that begin with a realistic, peaked size distribution, as expected from grain growth predictions. Our 3D numerical simulations directly form planetesimals via the gravitational collapse of pebble clouds. Models with multiple grain sizes show spatially distinct dust populations.

arxiv-2309-09274.title: Leveraging Social Discourse to Measure Check-worthiness of Claims for Fact-checking Journal: Information Processing and Management
arxiv-2309-09274.creator: Megha Sundriyal 1 , Md Shad Akhtar 1 , and Tanmoy Chakraborty 2
arxiv-2309-09274.description: Abstract The expansion of online social media platforms has led to a surge in online content consumption. However, this has also paved the way for disseminating false claims and misinformation. As a result, there is an escalating demand for a substantial workforce to sift through and validate such unverified claims. Currently, these claims are manually verified by fact-checkers.

arxiv-2403-02612.title: Modification to the Jeans criterion by external tides: Anisotropic fragmentation and formation of filaments 2020 Modification to the Jeans criterion by external tides: Anisotropic fragmentation and formation of filaments – References
arxiv-2403-02612.creator: Guang-Xing Li
arxiv-2403-02612.description: Abstract The Jeans criterion sets the foundation of our understanding of gravitational collapse. Jog studied the fragmentation of gas under external tides and derived a dispersion relation l ′ = l Jeans ​ 1 ( 1 + λ 0 ′ / 4 ​ π ​ G ​ ρ 0 ) 1 / 2 . l^{\prime}=l_{\rm Jeans}\frac{1}{(1+\lambda_{0}^{\prime}/4\pi G\rho_{0})^{1/2}}\;.

arxiv-2409-04960.title: Thermodynamics of Spin-Imbalanced Fermi Gases with SU ⁡ ( N ) \mathrm{SU}(N) Symmetric Interaction
arxiv-2409-04960.creator: Chengdong He, Xin-Yuan Gao, Ka Kwan Pak, Yu-Jun Liu, Peng Ren, Mengbo Guo, Entong Zhao, Yangqian Yan, Gyu-Boong Jo
arxiv-2409-04960.description: Abstract Thermodynamics of degenerate Fermi gases has been extensively studied through various aspects such as Pauli blocking effects, collective modes, BCS superfluidity, and more. Despite this, multi-component fermions with imbalanced spin configurations remain largely unexplored, particularly beyond the two-component scenario.

arxiv-2409-17230.title: Detecting axion dynamics on the surface of magnetic topological insulators
arxiv-2409-17230.creator: Zhi-Qiang Gao, Taige Wang, Michael P. Zaletel, Dung-Hai Lee
arxiv-2409-17230.description: Abstract Axions, initially proposed to solve the strong CP problem, have recently gained attention in condensed matter physics, particularly in topological insulators. However, detecting axion dynamics has proven challenging, with no experimental confirmations to date. In this study, we identify the surface of magnetic topological insulators as an ideal platform for observing axion dynamics.

arxiv-2503-08592.title: There’s more to life in reflected light: Simulating the detectability of a range of molecules for high-contrast, high-resolution observations of non-transiting terrestrial exoplanets Journal: PSJ
arxiv-2503-08592.creator: Miles H. Currie, Victoria S. Meadows
arxiv-2503-08592.description: Abstract The upcoming extremely large telescopes will provide the first opportunity to search for signs of habitability and life on non-transiting terrestrial exoplanets using high-contrast, high-resolution instrumentation. However, the suite of atmospheric gases in terrestrial exoplanet environments that are accessible to ground-based reflected light observations has not been thoroughly explored.

arxiv-2509-24556.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in Action: Real-Time Control of Vortex-Induced Vibrations
arxiv-2509-24556.creator: Hussam Sababha, Bernat Font, Mohammed Daqaq
arxiv-2509-24556.description: Abstract This study showcases an experimental deployment of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for active flow control (AFC) of vortex-induced vibrations (VIV) in a circular cylinder at a high Reynolds number ( R ​ e = 3000 Re=3000 ) using rotary actuation.

arxiv-2510-02983.title: Oracle-based Uniform Sampling from Convex Bodies
arxiv-2510-02983.creator: Thanh Dang, Jiaming Liang
arxiv-2510-02983.description: Abstract We propose new Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms to sample a uniform distribution on a convex body K K . Our algorithms are based on the Alternating Sampling Framework/proximal sampler, which uses Gibbs sampling on an augmented distribution and assumes access to the so-called restricted Gaussian oracle (RGO).

arxiv-2510-26387.title: Robust Welfare under Imperfect Competition
arxiv-2510-26387.creator: Konstantin von Beringe, Mark Whitmeyer
arxiv-2510-26387.description: Abstract We study welfare analysis for policy changes when supply behavior is only partially known. We augment the robust-demand approach of Kang and Vasserman 2025 with two supply primitives–intervals of feasible pass-through and conduct (market-power) parameters–applied to two equilibrium snapshots. A simple accounting identity distills the supply-side contribution to welfare to a simple integral expression.

arxiv-2511-09345.title: Seer Self-Consistency: Advance Budget Estimation for Adaptive Test-Time Scaling
arxiv-2511-09345.creator: Shiyu Ji, Yixuan Wang, Yijun Liu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che
arxiv-2511-09345.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shiyu Ji, Yixuan Wang, Yijun Liu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che. Test-time scaling improves the inference performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) but also incurs substantial computational costs. Although recent studies have reduced token consumption through dynamic self-consistency, they remain constrained by the high latency of sequential requests. In this paper, we propose SeerSC, a dynamic self-consistency framework that simultaneously improves token efficiency and latency by integrating System 1 and System 2 reasoning.

arxiv-2601-22298.title: Conformal Prediction for Generative Models via Adaptive Cluster-Based Density Estimation
arxiv-2601-22298.creator: Qidong Yang, Julie Zhu, Jonathan Giezendanner, Youssef Marzouk, Stephen Bates, Sherrie Wang
arxiv-2601-22298.description: Abstract Conditional generative models map input variables to complex, high-dimensional distributions, enabling realistic sample generation in a diverse set of domains. A critical challenge with these models is the absence of calibrated uncertainty, which undermines trust in individual outputs for high-stakes applications.

europmc-pmc6026004.title: JAK1/2 inhibition with baricitinib in the treatment of autoinflammatory interferonopathies.
europmc-pmc6026004.creator: Sanchez GAM, Reinhardt A, Ramsey S, Wittkowski H, Hashkes PJ, Berkun Y, Schalm S, Murias S, Dare JA, Brown D, Stone DL, Gao L, Klausmeier T, Foell D, de Jesus AA, Chapelle DC, Kim H, Dill S, Colbert RA, Failla L, Kost B, O'Brien M, Reynolds JC, Folio LR, Calvo KR, Paul SM, Weir N, Brofferio A, Soldatos A, Biancotto A, Cowen EW, Digiovanna JJ, Gadina M, Lipton AJ, Hadigan C, Holland SM, Fontana J, Alawad AS, Brown RJ, Rother KI, Heller T, Brooks KM, Kumar P, Brooks SR, Waldman M, Singh HK, Nickeleit V, Silk M, Prakash A, Janes JM, Ozen S, Wakim PG, Brogan PA, Macias WL, Goldbach-Mansky R.
europmc-pmc6026004.description: Background Monogenic IFN-mediated autoinflammatory diseases present in infancy with systemic inflammation, an IFN response gene signature, inflammatory organ damage, and high mortality. We used the JAK inhibitor baricitinib, with IFN-blocking activity in vitro, to ameliorate dis

pmc-10625179.title: A randomized trial evaluating the association between related gene polymorphism and nausea and vomiting induced by cisplatin multi-day chemotherapy
pmc-10625179.creator: Yilan Jin, Feng Chen, Juan Zhao, Ying Jiang, Gaowa Jin, Zewei Zhang, Quanfu Li
pmc-10625179.description: PurposeWe aim to investigate the correlation between gene polymorphisms and cisplatin chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), which was prevented by olanzapine or aprepitant triple antiemetic regimen.MethodsBefore chemotherapy, the blood samples of 89 malignant tumor patients who received multi-day chemotherapy with cisplatin were collected for sequencing and typing.

pmc-11430035.title: Multi-Strategy Improved Harris Hawk Optimization Algorithm and Its Application in Path Planning
pmc-11430035.creator: Chaoli Tang, Wenyan Li, Tao Han, Lu Yu, Tao Cui
pmc-11430035.description: Path planning is a key problem in the autonomous navigation of mobile robots and a research hotspot in the field of robotics. Harris Hawk Optimization (HHO) faces challenges such as low solution accuracy and a slow convergence speed, and it easy falls into local optimization in path planning applications.

pmc-11454198.title: 12567 Hybrid Closed-loop Insulin Pumps' Role In CFRD Management: A Retrospective Case Series Analysis
pmc-11454198.creator: Ibrahim Yaseen, David Slattery
pmc-11454198.description: Disclosure: I. Yaseen: None. D. Slattery: None.Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD) significantly burdens individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF), notably influencing their health longevity and quality of life. This case series retrospectively examines the effects of hybrid closed-loop (HCL) insulin pump therapy on CFRD management strategies.

pmc-12474458.title: Probing Viral Dark Matter: Comparative Genomics of Atypical Bacillus Phage YungSlug
pmc-12474458.creator: Allison A Johnson, Andrew Hale, Amine Sehnouni, Zainab Gbadamosi, Bret M Boyd, Bert Ely
pmc-12474458.description: Bacillus phage YungSlug is a novel phage with a genome that has limited homology to known viruses. To better understand this unique phage, we searched for close relatives of YungSlug using traditional comparative genomics approaches and a broad search of a large protein database.

pmc-12731193.title: Blood Donor RBC Genotyping at the National Advisory Unit on Immunohematology at Oslo University Hospital
pmc-12731193.creator: Inger Margit Alm, Hoyi Wong, Monica Stensrud, Geir Tomter, Mette S Bævre, Çiğdem Akalın Akkök, Chak-Sum Ho
pmc-12731193.description: Background: Blood transfusion has an essential place in the treatment of several patient groups but entails alloimmunization risk. The provision of phenotype-matched packed red blood cell concentrates (PRBCCs) is recommended for preventing alloimmunization in lifetime transfusion-dependent patients, while antigen-negative PRBCCs are a prerequisite for patients that already have blood group antibodies against clinically significant antigens.

pmc-13037890.title: HairTime: A noninvasive assay for estimating circadian phase from a single hair sample
pmc-13037890.creator: Bert Maier, Luísa K. Pilz, Selin Özcakir, Ali Rahjouei, Ashraf N. Abdo, Jan de Zeeuw, Dieter Kunz, Achim Kramer
pmc-13037890.description: SignificanceCircadian timing varies widely among individuals, influencing sleep, behavior, and health. However, assessing individual circadian phase outside laboratory settings remains difficult because gold-standard methods such as dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) are invasive and time-consuming. We developed HairTime, a simple, noninvasive assay that estimates circadian phase from a single hair sample. In an independent validation study, HairTime closely matched DLMO estimates.

pmc-13217072.title: Ophthalmic artery angioplasty in a cohort of patients with geographic atrophy secondary to non-exudative age-related macular degeneration
pmc-13217072.creator: Pedro Lylyk, Ivan Lylyk, Pedro N Lylyk, Carlos Bleise, Esteban Scrivano, Javier Lundquist, Rodolfo Nella-Castro, Nicolas Perez, Jeff Franco, Michael W Calhoun, Luana R Wilbur, Philip J Rosenfeld, Mario J Saravia
pmc-13217072.description: BackgroundThere is increasing evidence that vascular disease and chronic perfusion deficits play a role in the progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). This controlled clinical study evaluated the safety and feasibility of treating patients with late-stage AMD and associated geographic atrophy (GA). In addition, exploratory endpoints evaluated the potential to disrupt the disease process and initiate functional changes.

pmc-13254820.title: Evaluation of Metal Nanoparticles Using ICP‐OES in Hairs of Patients With Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia and Comparison With Control Group
pmc-13254820.creator: Farnaz Ahmadpour, Yalda Nahidi, Ali Ahmadpour, Naser Tayyebi Meibodi, Maryam Emadzadeh
pmc-13254820.description: BackgroundFrontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA) is an increasingly prevalent scarring alopecia potentially linked to environmental factors such as nanoparticles (NPs) in skincare and sunscreens.ObjectivesThis case–control study aimed to quantify titanium, zinc, aluminum, and iron concentrations in hair shafts of FFA patients versus controls using inductively coupled plasma‐optical emission spectrometry (ICP‐OES).
